_comment: Ships committed with REPLACE_WITH_* placeholders only. Fill in real credentials for a live Tier 2 setup — NEVER commit the real values. Real credentials belong in a gitignored .env file. This file is not in .gitignore because the placeholder version is safe to commit; treat your filled-in copy as sensitive.

cms._comment_platform: Which connector cms_publish.py uses by default. One of "wordpress" or "webflow". Override per-run with --platform.

wordpress._help: Application Passwords, not your login password: WordPress Admin -> Users -> Your Profile -> Application Passwords -> Add New Application Password. Requires WordPress 5.6+ (built in) or the Application Passwords plugin on older self-hosted sites. The account needs at least the Author role to create draft posts. yoast_meta_field is optional — set it to "_yoast_wpseo_metadesc" if the site runs Yoast and exposes that meta key on the REST API; leave blank otherwise (the meta description still gets written to the post excerpt).

webflow._help: Generate a v2 Site API token at Webflow -> Site settings -> Apps & Integrations -> API access (scope: CMS read+write). collection_id is the target CMS collection's ID (e.g. Blog Posts) — find it via GET https://api.webflow.com/v2/sites/{site_id}/collections. field_map maps this script's fields to your collection's actual field slugs, which vary per site/template; open the collection's field settings in Webflow if a publish attempt errors with an unrecognized-field message.

safety._comment: There is no flag here to publish live. Draft-only is enforced in code, not by this file: marketing-os-infra/lib/cms_connector.py always sends WordPress status=draft and Webflow isDraft=true, and neither function accepts a parameter that could change that. Taking a draft live is a separate, deliberate action you take by hand in the CMS admin.
